Del **9 al 11 de noviembre de 2026** se:
From **November 9 to 11, 2026**, the Rectorate of the University of Córdoba
hosts the [XII Meeting on Fundamental Cosmology](https://www.cosmo2026.com/),
the meeting of the network of Spanish groups working in cosmology.

The group is part of the organization: **Antonio José Cuesta** is the conference
chair and **Fernando Cornet** is a member of the local organizing committee (LOC).

The program covers the early Universe (inflation, cosmic microwave background,
reionization), large-scale structure and gravitational lensing,
theoretical cosmology and multi-messenger cosmology.

El proyecto internacional **HERON Coma P:
The international **HERON Coma Project**, led by **Javier Román**
together with R. Michael Rich (UCLA), has published in *Astronomy & Astrophysics* the
deepest image to date of the Coma cluster, one of the most massive galaxy groups
in the nearby Universe, about 300 million light-years away.

The image, the result of some **100 hours of observation** with the Jeanne Rich
telescope (71 cm, Lockwood Valley, California), shows the galaxies' stellar halos,
stellar streams, tidal tails and the light floating between the galaxies of the
cluster. These structures are about 2,000 times fainter than the darkest night sky
and hold the imprint of the interactions and mergers that have shaped the
galaxies over time: their “fossil records.” All data and images are publicly available.

- Paper: Román et al. (2026), [“The HERON Coma Project: Exploring the
  low-surface-brightness frontiers in the Coma cluster”](https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202662310),
  *Astronomy & Astrophysics* 713.
- Full story (in Spanish) in [Cordópolis](https://cordopolis.eldiario.es/cordoba-hoy/sociedad/uco-revela-registros-fosiles-evolucion-galaxias-vision-profunda-cumulo-coma_1_13657182.html).
